claims.claim: Composition concerns the arrangement of people, objects, and setting within the frame of an image.
Framing and movement can alter compositional relationships and direct attention to different material within a shot or sequence.
Aspect ratio is the relation of a frame's width to its height and affects the available shape for arranging material.
Balance, symmetry, asymmetry, relative size, and negative space are useful descriptive tools for comparing visual relationships in a frame.
The rule of thirds divides an image into horizontal and vertical thirds and is a useful starting point for composition rather than a universal requirement.
Internal frames such as doorways or windows can help describe how a subject is visually enclosed or separated from surrounding space.
A defensible composition interpretation identifies visible relationships and patterns, then remains qualified rather than treating one arrangement as a fixed emotional code or proof of intent.
